prompt.brief: Design a secure credit-card payment platform that tokenizes card data, authorizes and captures transactions, detects fraud, handles retries, and reconciles with issuers and merchants.
successSignals: Keep PAN data inside a tokenization boundary and model authorization, capture, void, refund, dispute, and settlement as a state machine.
Use idempotency keys, issuer timeouts, an outbox, and reconciliation so retries cannot double-charge or lose a response.
Run risk checks within a bounded decision budget while sending richer fraud features and review work asynchronously.
Explain PCI scope, key management, ledger correctness, webhooks, partial failure, chargebacks, and audit evidence.

functional: Tokenize payment methods, authorize purchases, capture or void funds, issue refunds, and expose transaction status.
Apply fraud and velocity controls, notify merchants, process issuer webhooks, and reconcile processor settlement files.
Support idempotent retries, merchant permissions, audit trails, disputes, key rotation, and limited data retention.
nonFunctional: Target p95 payment response below 2 seconds while preserving a durable state transition for every attempt.
Handle millions of transactions per day with merchant and account partitioning and issuer-specific rate limits.
Never double-capture or lose a settlement; use conditional transitions, idempotency, and daily reconciliation.
Return an explicit pending state when an issuer times out instead of guessing success or failure.
scaleAssumptions: Process 10 million payment attempts per day across 100,000 merchants and multiple processors.
Partition by merchant and transaction ID; isolate high-volume merchants and processor outage queues.
Retain tokenized transaction state, signed processor messages, ledger entries, and reconciliation evidence under policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Secure credit-card payment platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Secure credit-card payment platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Secure credit-card payment platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Secure credit-card payment platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Secure credit-card payment platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Secure credit-card payment platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Secure credit-card payment platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Secure credit-card payment platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Secure credit-card payment platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines authorization/capture, tokenization, ledger effects, settlement, scale, and failure contracts.
Entities and payment/merchant/network keys support secure card processing, fraud, settlement, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Secure credit-card payment platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
